reason: H0 only passes bytes to legacy ares_parse_*_reply functions and contains no TLSA-specific call, generic DNS-record parse/write exercise, RR-key access, or parse/serialize lifecycle. S1 adds full ARES_REC_TYPE_TLSA handling with three one-byte fields, required nonempty binary ARES_RR_TLSA_DATA, owned allocation, accessors, freeing, and serialization. Those length boundaries, ownership transitions, and round-trip behavior are fuzz-worthy and are not directly covered by H0.
evidence: ares_dns_parse_rr_data now dispatches ARES_REC_TYPE_TLSA to the new ares_dns_parse_rr_tlsa.

ares_dns_parse_rr_tlsa consumes ARES_RR_TLSA_CERT_USAGE, ARES_RR_TLSA_SELECTOR, and ARES_RR_TLSA_MATCH, computes remaining data from rdlength, rejects len == 0, duplicates attacker-controlled bytes, and transfers them through ares_dns_rr_set_bin_own.
ares_dns_write_rr now dispatches TLSA records to ares_dns_write_rr_tlsa, which rejects NULL or zero-length ARES_RR_TLSA_DATA and appends variable-length binary data.
ares_dns_rr_data_ptr and ares__dns_rr_free add TLSA binary-length and ownership handling through r.tlsa.data and r.tlsa.data_len.

H0 invokes ares_parse_a_reply, ares_parse_aaaa_reply, ares_parse_ptr_reply, ares_parse_ns_reply, ares_parse_srv_reply, ares_parse_mx_reply, ares_parse_txt_reply, ares_parse_soa_reply, ares_parse_naptr_reply, ares_parse_caa_reply, and ares_parse_uri_reply, but no TLSA or DNS-record writer path.
recommended_action: Add a harness path that parses DNS records containing ARES_REC_TYPE_TLSA, exercises all four TLSA keys through the typed RR accessors, serializes the record through the DNS-record writer, reparses it, and frees it. Mutate truncated 0–3-byte RDATA, zero-length association data, inconsistent rdlength values, large binary data, arbitrary u8 field values, and valid parse/write/parse round trips.
